title: KPMG Canada client documents accessed in cybersecurity breach, accounting firm says

image.caption: Signage at the KPMG offices in Ottawa on June 28, 2024. The accounting firm says some client documents were accessed in a recent data breach. (Sean Kilpatrick/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: KPMG did not provide details about the breach, including the scope or nature of the attack. But a spokesperson says the company is confident that the accessed data is not available online, or being misused for any purpose.
A spokesperson says accounting firm is "confident" the data accessed is not available online, or being misused
KPMG Canada says some of its clients' tax documents were accessed in a cybersecurity breach.
The accounting firm did not provide details about the breach, including the scope or nature of the attack. KPMG says it is reaching out to clients who were affected.
Spokesperson Sonja Cloutier-Bosworth said on Thursday the company is confident that the accessed data is not available online or being misused for any purpose.
The Globe and Mail first reported the confirmation of the breach.
It's the latest in a string of cyberattacks targeting organizations in Canada, especially those in the legal and financial sectors.
Federal privacy commissioner investigating Crime Stoppers data breach

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security said in an alert last month that multiple firms had been targeted by scammers impersonating internal IT support, either over the phone or using Microsoft Teams calls in a process known as "vishing" (short for "voice phishing") or by directing employees to fake sign-in pages.

The vishing scam was behind data breached at four major law firms last month, according to the Globe and Mail's reporting. Bennett Jones LLP, McCarthy Tétrault LLP, Davies Ward Phillips & Vineberg LLP and Borden Ladner Gervais LLP all had portions of their data, including client files, accessed as a result of the data breaches.
